text:
alice: CI red on publish for rdx/runner — push to mirror failing only in CI. Local docker push to registry.redwood.com works. Logs show: 'blob upload failed: digest mismatch (expected sha256:abc123... got sha256:def456...)'. Anyone seen this recently? CI: buildkite #2311

ci-bot: Pipeline failed: build 2311/publish. Logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/2311 (artifact: publish.log)

jess: are we sure it's not creds/permissions? digest mismatch usually means the layer tar changed between upload and manifest creation.

dan: what builder? kaniko, buildkit, docker?

alice: kaniko v1.8 on our buildkite agents. Dockerfile had a tiny change in final stage: created a symlink to node_modules (ln -s ...) — might be unrelated but correlated timing.

marc: odd. If kaniko packs files differently (mtime, pax headers) the gziped layer digest can change. local docker push using docker daemon often produces different tar gzip bytes but same digest normally. did you compare the layer tar from CI vs local?

jess: I pulled the layer tar from the kaniko workspace artifact and ran:
```
sha256sum layer.tar.gz
sha256sum layer-unpacked.tar
```
Digest from manifest != sha256 of tar. Also retried with kaniko v1.9 and got same mismatch.

dan: could registry be recompressing the layer or altering headers? that would be wild. Also check if multipart uploads retried and finalized with different order.

infra-bot: infra-bot: I checked registry logs around the failure time. No key rotation. There was an S3 put-object retry spike at ~13:07 UTC (increased 5xx from S3 gateway) which caused several multipart finalize retries.

marc: S3 retries shouldn't change content bytes. Another possibility: symlink in image causes different tar ordering between builders, and kaniko's snapshot algorithm produce a different layer digest than what's referenced in the manifest kaniko constructs (bug?).

jess: there's also an option in kaniko to normalize timestamps/uid/gid for reproducible archives (experimental). try building with --reproducible or --single-snapshot to see if digests stabilize.

alice: ok queued a rerun with kaniko --reproducible, no-cache off. If that passes we'll know it's about non-reproducible metadata.

dan: I'm going to bisect the Dockerfile change: revert the symlink commit and rerun publish. @marc can you watch registry logs during rerun?

marc: watching. queuing local docker push for comparison as well.

jess: rerun with kaniko --reproducible started.

ci-bot: Rerun started: build 2311/retry-1.

dan: quick note — local docker push (same built image tar) succeeded to internal mirror. So builder path seems to matter.

marc: registry logs during the failing run show regular PUTs and Finalize. No content transformation. S3 had a spike but not correlated to successful pushes from other builds.

jess: rerun finished — publish step succeeded with --reproducible. That strongly points to non-deterministic metadata (mtime/owner) changing digest.

dan: bisect done: reverting symlink commit made the original pipeline succeed without --reproducible. So symlink creation changed how kaniko snapshots the layer tar (ordering/metadata), producing a tar that doesn't match the manifest digest kaniko recorded earlier in the run.

alice: summary: root cause is non-reproducible layer metadata when symlink present + kaniko snapshotting behavior -> digest mismatch on manifest finalization. Workaround: enable kaniko --reproducible (or single-snapshot) in our buildkite image publish step. Longer term: upgrade kaniko and add a tiny CI test that does a publish to mirror for this Dockerfile pattern.

marc: I'll open an infra PR to flip the flag in our shared pipeline and upgrade kaniko to the latest stable.

alice: I'll open a small app PR to remove the symlink or make it created in a reproducible way if possible. Also adding CI test to catch regressions. PRs: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/402 and https://git.internal/redwood/rdx/pulls/88

jess: :thumbsup: thanks everyone. Filing a short postmortem note in #postmortems after we validate the fix.

alice: Thanks — closing this thread once infra PR merges.
